_meta.indication: Treatment of uncomplicated urinary tract infections (uUTI) caused by the designated microorganisms Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, or Proteus mirabilis in adult women who have limited or no alternative oral antibacterial treatment options

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled noninferiority trial, 1:1 randomization, vs amoxicillin/clavulanate; NI margin of 10%
pivotal_trials.population: Adult women with uncomplicated urinary tract infection (uUTI)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall success (clinical and microbiologic combined) at test of cure (TOC), Day 12
pivotal_trials.result: In the micro-MITTS population, overall response was 296/480 (61.7%) for sulopenem vs 243/442 (55.0%) for amoxicillin/clavulanate; difference 6.7% (95% CI, 0.3, 13.0; p=0.040) — noninferior and superior

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled trial, 1:1 randomization, vs ciprofloxacin
pivotal_trials.population: Adult women with uncomplicated urinary tract infection (uUTI)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall success (clinical and microbiologic combined) at test of cure (TOC), Day 12
pivotal_trials.result: In ciprofloxacin-nonsusceptible pathogens (micro-MITTR), sulopenem superior: overall response 77/160 (48%) vs ciprofloxacin 49/149 (33%), difference 15% (95% CI 4.4%, 26.1%; p=0.0062). In ciprofloxacin-susceptible (micro-MITTS), sulopenem inferior: 218/365 (60%) vs 296/410 (72%), difference -12.5% (95% CI -19.1%, -5.9%)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%): diarrhea, nausea, vulvovaginal mycotic infection, headache, and vomiting. In Trial 310, TEAEs occurred in 18.9% of sulopenem subjects vs 12.3% of amoxicillin/clavulanate, driven by diarrhea (8.1% vs 4.1%). Warnings/precautions include hypersensitivity reactions, C. difficile-associated diarrhea, risk of uric acid kidney stones, and exacerbation of gout.
target_moa: Sulopenem is a penem (beta-lactam) antibacterial that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), with highest affinity for PBP2; it is bactericidal. Probenecid is a renal tubular transport inhibitor that increases sulopenem systemic exposure.
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination: penem antibacterial prodrug sulopenem etzadroxil + probenecid)

advisory_committee.vote: The Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee met September 9, 2024; there were no voting questions.

basis.text: Sulopenem was granted fast track designation for uUTI, cUTI, and cIAI on March 15, 2019.

citations.quote: The Division granted sulopenem qualified infectious disease product designation for uUTI, cUTI, and cIAI on 29 Jul 2016 and fast track designation for these same indications on 15 Mar 2019.

basis.text: The resubmitted NDA 213972 (received April 25, 2024) was designated Priority Review.
Sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid was granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation for uUTI, cUTI, and cIAI on July 29, 2016 (bilayer tablet QIDP granted October 27, 2017).

citations.quote: The Division granted sulopenem QIDP designation for the treatment of uUTIs, complicated urinary tract infections (cUTIs), and complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAIs) on July 29, 2016, as well as fast track designation for these indications on March 15, 2019.

On October 27, 2017, PF-03709270/probenecid (sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid) bilayer tablet was granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation for uUTI, complicated urinary tract infection (cUTI), and complicated intra-abdominal infection (cIAI) and Fast Track designation for these same indications on March 15, 2019.

summary.text: 505(b)(2) NDA for an oral penem antibacterial fixed-dose combination; QIDP- and fast-track-designated, reviewed under Priority Review. Originally submitted in 2020, it received a complete response in July 2021, then was resubmitted April 25, 2024 with a new uUTI trial (Trial 310) and was taken to the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee before traditional approval.

citations.quote: On April 25, 2024, the 505(b)(2) NDA 213972 for sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid oral tablet, a bilayer fixed-dose combination of the penem antibacterial prodrug sulopenem etzadroxil and probenecid (500 mg; 500 mg), a renal tubular transport inhibitor, was resubmitted by Iterum Therapeutics US Ltd.

Prior to the original submission of NDA 213972 in 2020, three phase 3 trials were completed - IT001-301 (Trial 301) for uUTI utilizing oral sulopenem, IT001-302 (Trial 302) for cUTI, and IT001-303 (Trial 303) for cIAI, each utilizing IV to oral
The NDA received a complete response on July 23, 2021, due to lack of substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) for sulopenem for the treatment of uUTI.

Because sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid will, if approved, be the first oral penem antibacterial drug on the U.S. market, the NDA was taken to the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee on September 9, 2024
